# ArmorBreak · 破甲
**Evidence-first security analysis for AI agents.**
*Inspect with tools. Enforce scope in code. Keep the evidence.*
ArmorBreak is an open-source toolkit for **authorized** reverse engineering, source-code review, pac
ket analysis, digital forensics, and security research. One host-neutral Core powers **DeepSeek Harn
ess**, **MCP-capable agents**, and **standalone Node.js integrations**. Models can help plan and int
erpret; they do **not** grant permission to act.
**Download Stable** · **Quick start** · **Integrations** · **Release verification** · **Documentatio
table** · **Quick start** · **Integrations** · **Release verification** · **Documentation** · **中文**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **V2.2.0 Stable is published.** It covers a **Verified Core** and **Experimental Pr
ovider Integrations**. Commercial OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini endpoints remain `LIVE_UNVERIFIED`;
AI-assisted security review is not human certification. The historical **Full GA** contract remains
`gaReady:false` with 18 blockers. Read release verification and scope/limitations before relying on

> [!NOTE]
> **V2.3.1 is the active Stable release candidate.** V2.3.0 remains an unpublished histori
cal candidate whose protected Tag Gate failed; its Tag and failure history are retained. V2.3.1 targ
ets the Windows upgrade/rollback gate repair. It is not available as Stable until its public release
page and exact assets are verified. The owner-approved implementation-agent self-review policy does
not claim independent human security or legal certification. See V2.3.1 release notes, V2.3.0 histo
rical notes, and portable install requirements.
## Why ArmorBreak?
| The challenge | The design |
| Agent integrations reinvent execution | **One Core** behind DSH, MCP, CLI, and application APIs |
| Model output gets confused with permission | **Policy and operator approval** live outside the mod

el |
| Findings are hard to reproduce | **Task-scoped evidence, hashes, findings, and reports** |
|
First use assumes a paid model | **Offline L0 analysis**, with optional model integrations |
ArmorBreak is a **research toolkit**, not a guarantee that a target is vulnerable or a substitute fo
r independent security assessment.

## Scope and limitations
- **46 capabilities / 8 domains** in the recorded registry: **44 L0, 1 L1, 1 L2**; **L3 denied**. Re

gistration is not a promise that every optional external analyzer is installed.
- **9 workflows; 7 D
SH Skills; 10 DSH model tools; 7 MCP tools.** These are different interfaces and must not be added i

nto one tool count.
- **12 host entries / 10 L0 / 9 third-party L0** in the current matrix; each hos
t retains its own evidence level. Claude Code MCP and Claude Cowork CLI, Gemini CLI and Antigravity

are separate rows.
- **Verified Core:** Universal Core, MCP server, Skills, Offline Golden, recorded

local-model verification, and the installer/migration/rollback paths covered by the release CI.
- *
*Experimental Provider Integrations:** OpenAI-compatible, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, and

Gemini Native are `LIVE_UNVERIFIED`; mock and local results do not certify commercial endpoints.
- *
*Historical Full GA:** `gaReady:false`, 18 blockers. Stable is a separate, owner-approved release co

ntract and does not waive Full GA.
- **AI review:** four AI-assisted rounds completed initial review
; findings still require remediation/retest. This is not an independent human audit or certification

.
- **Provenance:** GitHub OIDC/Sigstore attests build origin and subject binding; it is not a secur
ity certification or production code signature.
**Risk levels:** L0 is local/offline; L1 requires usable isolation and platform approval; L2 require
s authorized scope and platform approval; L3 is always denied. See security policy, Stable policy, a
scope and platform approval; L3 is always denied. See security policy, Stable policy, and GA review.

[代码示例省略，未执行]

roval.
2. **A finding is not proof of exploitation.** Facts, hypotheses, and unverified leads are se

parated.
3. **A protocol mock is not a live-provider result.** Model routing and analysis authorizat
ion remain separate.
